rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic opening restricts the acts of sending down and preserving to God, answering the rejecters' mockery and demand for angels in the preceding context.
rows.anchor: صدر الآية مسوق سوق الحصر، وظاهر السياق أن الحصر ناظر إلى ما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an came gradually from God, not from Muhammad or angels; God's complete care preserves this living, enduring remembrance forever.
rows.anchor: لم تأت به أنت من عندك حتى يعجزوك ويبطلوه بعنادهم وشدة بطشهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine preservation bars additions, omissions, and changes of form or wording that would erase the Qur'an's identity as God's remembrance.
rows.anchor: مصون من الزيادة عليه بما يبطل به كونه ذكرا، مصون من النقص كذلك، مصون من التغيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fussilat likewise calls the Qur'an an invulnerable book that falsehood cannot approach, corroborating its divine protection from distortion.
rows.anchor: إن الذين كفروا بالذكر لما جاءهم وإنه لكتاب عزيز لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in dhikr is anaphoric, and the active participle lāḥifūn denotes future preservation, as its form ordinarily indicates.
rows.anchor: أن اللام في الذكر للعهد الذكري وأن المراد بالوصف لحافظون هو الاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that Torah and Gospel are also called remembrance overlooks context: this promise concerns the Qur'an after its revelation and does not make remembrance itself the cause of preservation.
rows.anchor: لا دلالة فيها على علية الذكر للحفظ الإلهي ودوران الحكم مداره

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits from Imam al-Sadiq that on Judgment Day a herald will admit only Muslims to Paradise, when disbelievers will wish they had been Muslims; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إذا كان يوم القيامة نادى مناد من عند الله لا يدخل الجنة إلا مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the command to leave the rejecters, their hopes are what distract them; they will soon know the outcome.
rows.anchor: { ذرهم يأكلوا ويتمتعوا ويلههم الأمل } أي شغلهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits from Abd Allah ibn Ata al-Makki that al-Baqir and al-Sadiq gave a similar explanation of the verse; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: روى العياشي عن عبد الله بن عطاء المكي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام في تفسير الآية مثله

words: ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين
rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet saying sinful members of his community will be punished, mocked by polytheists, then every monotheist will be brought out of Hell; the Prophet recited this verse. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh transmit it with a sound chain.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وأبو سعيد الخدري وأنس بن مالك
rows.claim: The same meaning is also transmitted from Abu Musa al-Ashari, Abu Said al-Khudri, and Anas ibn Malik from the Prophet; no grading is stated here.
rows.anchor: هذا المعنى مروي بطرق أخرى عن أبي موسى الاشعري وأبي سعيد الخدري وأنس بن مالك عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

words: ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين
rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali reports the Prophet describing sinful monotheists' graded punishments and eventual extraction from Hell into Paradise; after disbelievers are left behind, their fate illustrates the verse. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truthuth is a plant, and ḥamīl al-sayl means the debris carried by a flood, glossing the preceding report's imagery.
rows.anchor: الطرثوث نبت وحميل السيل غثاؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that Shia transmissions contain reports close in meaning to the preceding narration; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقد روي من طرق الشيعة ما يقرب من الحديث مضمونا

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh transmit Abu Said's report that the Prophet used three planted sticks to compare a person, his term, and his hope, which death cuts short; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: أخرج أحمد وابن مردويه عن أبي سعيد

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A report with approximately the same meaning is also transmitted from Anas from the Prophet; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وروي ما يقرب من معناه بطرق عن أنس عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali says he most fears following desire, which turns one from truth, and long hopes, which make one forget the afterlife.
rows.anchor: عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أنه قال ان اخوف ما أخاف عليكم اثنان

rows.speaker: عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits the explanation that if angels had been sent down, the people would have received no further respite and would have perished; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام لو أنزلنا بالملائكة لم ينظروا وهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historical record establishes that Muhammad claimed prophethood, preached to a community, and brought a book he called the Qur'an and attributed to God; today's Qur'an is generally that same book, not a lost text replaced wholesale.
rows.anchor: من ضروريات التاريخ أن النبي العربي محمدا صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم جاء قبل أربعة عشر قرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some proponents allege only limited additions, omissions, or textual changes, while accepting that most of the revealed book remains as it was in the Prophet's time.
rows.anchor: وإنما احتمل بعض من قال به من المخالف أو المؤالف زيادة شيء يسير كالجملة أو الآية أو النقص أو التغيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extant Qur'an retains the challenge of unique eloquence throughout its verses, with a striking structure unmatched by preserved or reported Arabic speech.
rows.anchor: فنجده يتحدى بالبلاغة والفصاحة ونجد ما بأيدينا مشتملا على ذلك النظم العجيب البديع لا يعدله ولا يشابهه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's challenge that it contains no contradiction is fulfilled by the present text: other verses resolve apparent ambiguities and conflicts.
rows.anchor: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an also challenges all humans and jinn to produce its like and calls itself decisive speech without jest; the extant text meets these challenges.
rows.anchor: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text gives clear truth and guidance to rational principles, natural laws, and moral virtues; its many teachings are unified by tawhid, into which they resolve and from which they derive.
rows.anchor: بل نجد جميع المعارف على سعتها وكثرتها حية بحياة واحدة مدبرة بروح واحد هو مبدء جميع المعارف القرآنية والأصل الذي إليه ينتهي الجميع ويرجع وهو التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic accounts of earlier prophets and peoples preserve the purity of religion and prophetic servitude; comparison with corresponding accounts in the two Testaments makes this evident.
rows.anchor: يفصل القول فيها على ما يليق بطهارة الدين ويناسب نزاهة ساحة النبوة وخلوصها للعبودية والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an reports future events explicitly or allusively, and the text in hand confirms those predictions as true.
rows.anchor: يورد آيات في الملاحم ويخبر عن الحوادث الآتية في آيات كثيرة بالتصريح أو بالتلويح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an describes itself as light and guidance to a straight path and the most upright religion; the extant text loses none of its guidance.
rows.anchor: يصف نفسه بأنه نور وأنه هاد يهدي إلى صراط مستقيم وإلى الملة التي هي أقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr is among the Qur'an's most comprehensive descriptions: it recalls God, His names, attributes and acts, angels, scriptures, messengers, laws, resurrection, and human destinies in Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: أنه ذكر لله فإنه يذكر به تعالى بما أنه آية دالة عليه حية خالدة، وبما أنه يصفه بأسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present Qur'an loses none of the meanings of remembrance: its many teachings all recall God and constitute the purpose of calling it dhikr.
rows.anchor: ففي جميع ذلك ذكر الله، وهو الذي يرومه القرآن بإطلاق القول بأنه ذكر ونجد ما بأيدينا من القرآن لا يفقد شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fussilat says falsehood cannot prevail over or enter the Qur'an at any time through nullification, abrogation, or distortion that would erase its character as remembrance.
rows.anchor: لا يغلبه باطل ولا يدخل فيه حالا، ولا في مستقبل الزمان لا بإبطال ولا بنسخ ولا بتغيير أو تحريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted wording of remembrance and preservation means God protects the Qur'an against any addition, omission, or change of wording or order that would destroy its remembrance of Him.
rows.anchor: فقد أطلق الذكر وأطلق الحفظ فالقرآن محفوظ بحفظ الله عن كل زيادة ونقيصة وتغيير في اللفظ أو في الترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in lahu cannot refer to the Prophet: the context shows that the polytheists mocked him because of the Qur'an he claimed was revealed to him.
rows.anchor: ومن سخيف القول إرجاع ضمير " له " إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فإنه مدفوع بالسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed Qur'an is divinely guarded from additions, omissions, and changes, as promised to the Prophet; any alteration that erased its described qualities would have left visible effects, which the extant text lacks.
rows.anchor: فقد تبين مما فصلناه أن القرآن الذي أنزله الله على نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ووصفه بأنه ذكر محفوظ على ما أنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument rules out distortion that removes Qur'anic qualities, though a fallen repeated verse or a dot or inflection difference could be posited if it affects none of them.
rows.anchor: فلو فرض سقوط شيء منه أو تغير في إعراب أو حرف أو ترتيب وجب أن يكون في أمر لا يؤثر في شيء من أوصافه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The mutually transmitted hadith al-Thaqalayn says the Prophet left the Qur'an and his family, and that holding to both prevents misguidance; this makes reliance on a corrupted book incoherent.
rows.anchor: حديث الثقلين المتواتر من طرق الفريقين " إني تارك فيكم الثقلين كتاب الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
rows.claim: Numerous reports from the Prophet and the Imams command comparing reports with the Qur'an; their unrestricted wording makes them apply beyond legal verses.
rows.anchor: الأخبار الكثيرة الواردة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأئمه أهل البيت عليهم السلام الآمرة بعرض الأخبار على الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal to restrict comparison reports to legal traditions lacks a textual qualifier; fabrication also targets doctrine and prophetic history, as Israelite material illustrates.
rows.anchor: فتخصيصها بذلك تخصيص من غير مخصص. على أن لسان أخبار العرض كالصريح أو هو صريح

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
rows.claim: The Imams' use of verses matching today's Qur'an, including where isolated distortion reports exist, supports reading many phrases such as kadhā nuzila as explanatory interpretation rather than a variant text, contrasted with inner meaning and ta'wil.
rows.anchor: في الموارد التي فيها آحاد من الروايات بالتحريف، وهذا أحسن شاهد على أن المراد في كثير من روايات التحريف من قولهم عليهم السلام كذا نزل هو التفسير

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
rows.claim: Reports from Ali and his descendants say the Qur'an held by people is revealed by God despite differing from Ali's codex; their instruction to followers is to read as others do.
rows.anchor: ما بأيدي الناس قرآن نازل من عند الله سبحانه وإن كان غير ما ألفه علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports imply differences from Ali's codex concern only surah or verse order where meaning and the Qur'an's divinely described qualities are unaffected; together they establish preservation of those qualities.
rows.anchor: فإنما يخالفه في ترتيب السور أو في ترتيب بعض الآيات التي لا يؤثر اختلال ترتيبها في مدلولها شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Shia hadith scholars, Hashwiyya, and some Sunni hadith scholars held that Qur'anic distortion occurred by omission or textual reordering, but not by addition, as no Muslim was said to claim addition.
rows.anchor: ذهب جماعة من محدثي الشيعة والحشوية وجماعة من محدثي أهل السنة إلى وقوع التحريف بمعنى النقص والتغيير في اللفظ أو الترتيب دون الزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proponents cite numerous Shia and Sunni reports alleging that compilations under Abu Bakr and Uthman omitted or changed passages, words, and letters; some claim two thousand such reports, and al-Alusi calls them beyond count.
rows.anchor: الأخبار الكثيرة المروية من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة الدالة على سقوط بعض السور والآيات وكذا الجمل وأجزاء الجمل والكلمات والحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also cite differences among Ibn Masud's codex, Ubayy ibn Kab's, and Uthman's regional copies, varying counts and surah order, along with many anomalous readings transmitted from early Muslims.
rows.anchor: مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود المصحف المعروف مما ينيف على ستين موضعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second argument for loss says ordinary reasoning makes a complete, accurate compilation improbable when a non-infallible person gathers a scattered text.
rows.anchor: أن العقل يحكم بأنه إذا كان القرآن متفرقا متشتتا منتشرا عند الناس وتصدى لجمعه غير المعصوم يمتنع عادة

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A third argument says Ali withdrew after the Prophet's death, compiled the Qur'an, presented it as revelation, and was turned away in favor of Zayd's collection; proponents infer that his codex differed, citing his knowledge and a report that truth accompanies him.
rows.anchor: أن عليا عليه السلام اعتزل الناس بعد رحلة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ولم يرتد إلا للصلاة حتى جمع القرآن ثم حمله إلى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth argument infers that Muslims must have altered the Qur'an because earlier communities altered their scriptures and reports predict Muslims will imitate them.
rows.anchor: ما ورد من الروايات أنه يقع في هذه الأمة ما وقع في بني إسرائيل حذو النعل بالنعل والقذة بالقذة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Abu Said reports the Prophet's warning that Muslims will follow earlier peoples step by step, even into a lizard's hole; asked whether he meant Jews and Christians, he replies, who else? The author calls the report widely transmitted from numerous Companions.
rows.anchor: في صحيح البخاري عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال " لتتبعن سنن من كان قبلكم شبرا بشبر

rows.speaker: عدة من أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Mustafid Shia routes through several Imams transmit the same prediction and add that Islam's bonds will be undone one by one, beginning with trust and ending with prayer; no separate grading is given.
rows.anchor: من طرق الشيعة عن عدة من أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كما في تفسير القمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Consensus cannot establish absence of additions: it gives probable, not certain, belief, since accumulating agreeing opinions strengthens probability without turning it into certainty.
rows.anchor: الإجماع ليس في نفسه حجة عقلية يقينية بل هو عند القائلين باعتباره حجة شرعية لو أفاد شيئا من الاعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Sunnis consensus relies on a Prophetic report against communal error; for Shia it depends on an infallible Imam's inclusion or being inferred. Both depend on prophethood, whose living proof is the Qur'an, so possible distortion undermines the proof and consensus. Historical survival of a Qur'an in general does not prove each cited verse untouched.
rows.anchor: حجية الإجماع بالجملة متوقفة على صحة النبوة وذلك ظاهر، وصحة النبوة اليوم متوقفة على سلامة القرآن من التحريف المستوجب لزوال صفات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating distortion reports as authoritative traditions is circular for the same reason as consensus; as historical evidence they are isolated, conflicting, not mutawatir or decisive, and few are both sound in chain and conclusive in meaning.
rows.anchor: فلا يبقى للمستدل بها إلا أن يتمسك بها بما أنها أسناد ومصادر تاريخية وليس فيها حديث متواتر ولا محفوف بقرائن قطعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most such reports have broken or weak chains, and even rare reports sound in chain and meaning are not safe from fabrication or insertion, including Israelite material.
rows.anchor: فإن كثيرا مما وقع فيها من الآيات المحكية من قبيل التفسير وذكر معنى الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some alleged extra Qur'anic passages do not resemble Qur'anic style; even apart from that, reports contradicting the Qur'an are rejected.
rows.anchor: ومع الغض عن ذلك فهي تذكر من الآيات والسور ما لا يشبه النظم القرآني بوجه، ومع الغض عن جميع ذلك فإنها مخالفة للكتاب مردودة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأول
rows.claim: The author says many alleged variant passages are explanations rather than quotations of a corrupted verse, citing a Rawdat al-Kafi report from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal on 4:63; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: كما في روضة الكافي عن أبي الحسن الأول في قول الله " اولئك الذين يعلم الله ما في قلوبهم فأعرض عنهم
